Karen: Quick question — do we bump the patch for a docs-only change that only updates release notes and a README?
Sam: My read: semver-wise, docs-only doesn't change public behavior so shouldn't require a patch. But our release pipeline auto-increments if a PR merges to main.
Mihir: Right, the current CI rule is dumb: any merge to main triggers a patch bump script that looks at `git diff --name-only $base...$head` and checks changed files. It treats `docs/` as "touching" the release.
Lila: Could we change the rule to only bump when src/ or api/ or packaging files change? e.g., regex `^(src|api|pkg|internal|deploy)/`
Dan: I like that. Also want to call out edgecases: docs + tiny test fix that tweaks behavior. We need a clear list of globs not just a docs boolean.
Sam: Another option: add a commit footer `release: no-bump` that the bot parses. That covers one-off cases without changing glob logic.
Karen: I prefer the glob filter + allowlist for explicitness. `release: no-bump` feels easy to forget.
Mihir: Implementation detail: release-bot currently creates tag `v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}` and pushes. If we skip bump, the tag won't be created and the next real change will still create a patch.
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout for v1.12.4 (patch) — 4 hosts in us-west -> 10% -> streaming logs at https://deploys.redwood/1.12.4
Lila: If we go with allowlist globs, we should also add a safety for "docs+chore" where package.json changed only for devDependencies — that shouldn't bump.
Dan: Agree. For packaging files specifically, only bump if `dependencies` (not devDependencies) changed. We can parse `git show $commit:package.json` to diff the JSON keys.
Sam: How should we name rollback tags? We've had messy names like `v1.11.9-rollback` and then `v1.11.9-rollback-2` which confused the release dashboard. Proposal: use `v1.11.9+rollback.20270301` (buildmeta-style) or `v1.11.9-rcb1`? Thoughts?
Karen: I vote for `+rollback.YYYYMMDD` (buildmeta) — it keeps semver ordering and signals not-a-new-release semver-wise.
Mihir: Buildmeta is okay but some tools strip after `+`. Our release UI should map those to a visible label. Alternatively `-rollback.1` fits pre-release slot but sorts before.
Lila: We should also document rollback policy in RELEASES.md and show example commands:
```
# rollback one step
git tag v1.12.4-rollback.20270301
git push origin v1.12.4-rollback.20270301
release-bot --promote v1.12.4-rollback.20270301
```
Dan: Back to pinning: when we pin transitive deps in Dedicated builds, we add `+pin` in buildmeta and keep a pinned-deps manifest. That should be separate from semver.
Karen: Ok action items: 1) Mihir to PR glob-based bump filter (exclude docs, .md, changelog unless other code changed). 2) Sam to add commit-footer parsing as an override. 3) Lila to write RELEASES.md section about rollback tag conventions and operations. 4) Dan to draft package.json diff check for deps vs devDeps.
Sam: I'll also add a quick dashboard change to show "auto-bump reason" in the release list (files changed / commit footer).
